tier_reason: First-party bar charts (assets/cli-bench-results-1080p-amd-rx9700.png and siblings) produced by a public harness, scripts/src/benchmark_e2e.py with scripts/configs/benchmark_e2e.toml, which runs ffmpeg's nlmeans_opencl at its defaults (s=1, p=7, r=15) against av-denoise nlmeans at matched strength 1.0, patch radius 3 and search radius 7. It falls short of A because the host CPU, rustc version, FFmpeg version, GPU driver/Vulkan stack and test clips are not published; only the GPU (named RX9700 in the asset file names) is given.

corrections.language: Rust (GPU kernels JIT-compiled via CubeCL; CLI, crate and VapourSynth plugin)
corrections.baseline: FFmpeg libavfilter nlmeans_opencl (OpenCL NLMeans filter) at its defaults s=1, p=7, r=15; not hqdn3d or the CPU nlmeans filter. V-BM3D (vsdenoise, HIP) is a second, VapourSynth-only reference.
corrections.claimed_speedup: README text: around 2x FFmpeg's nlmeans_opencl at matched settings and about 1.3x faster than V-BM3DHIP. The 1080p 8-bit CLI chart (values read from the bars, approximate) shows av-denoise NLMeans at FFmpeg-matched settings about 116 fps, NLMeans-HQ defaults about 105 fps and NL4D defaults about 79.5 fps against FFmpeg NLMeans OpenCL about 10.6 fps, roughly 11x for the matched arm (derived from page data, chart reading). The 4K 10-bit CLI chart has no FFmpeg bar (ffmpeg's OpenCL NLMeans rejects 10-bit formats, per the config) and shows av-denoise at about 12.5-15.7 fps. In the VapourSynth-plugin charts NL4D is about 29 fps against V-BM3D FAST about 28 fps at 1080p and slightly slower than V-BM3D FAST at 4K (about 6.8 vs 7.6 fps), so the 1.3x V-BM3D claim is not visible in the charts.
corrections.workload: End-to-end wall-clock throughput (fps = probed frame count / wall time, including startup and scene detection, one repeat after a warmup run) on an unpublished 1080p 8-bit clip and a 4K 10-bit clip, output discarded to /dev/null. FFmpeg arm: ffmpeg decode, format=yuv420p, hwupload, nlmeans_opencl, hwdownload, -f null. av-denoise arm: target/release/av-denoise -A vulkan nlmeans --preset veryfast --strength 1.0 --patch-radius 3 --search-radius 7 --workers 2 (FFMS2 decode, y4m out, luma and chroma planes by default). V-BM3D arms run through vspipe on three profiles.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: av-denoise built with cargo build --release --bin av-denoise --features vulkan,binary (Justfile _build-benchmark-bin); no custom release profile; rustc version not stated; GPU kernels are JIT-compiled at runtime by CubeCL. FFmpeg build and version not stated.
corrections.hardware: AMD GPU named RX9700 in the chart file names; host CPU, driver and Vulkan/OpenCL stack not stated
corrections.stars_or_usage: 14 stars, 1 fork; crates.io av-denoise 0.5.0-alpha3 (395 downloads); VapourSynth plugin on PyPI as vsavd 0.4.1
corrections.caveats: The README text says about 2x at matched settings while the 1080p chart (added 2026-09-06 in commit 'Add benchmark graphics') shows roughly 11x; the two are not reconciled. Quality is not matched by any PSNR or SSIM measurement: the arms share the NLMeans algorithm and parameters, but output equivalence is not checked. The FFmpeg arm pays hwupload/hwdownload copies and runs one filter chain, while av-denoise runs two scene-parallel workers; both include decode and startup in wall time. Test clips, FFmpeg version, host CPU and drivers are unpublished, and the figures are images only. The 1.3x V-BM3D claim is not borne out by the VapourSynth-plugin charts (NL4D roughly ties V-BM3D FAST at 1080p and trails it at 4K). The baseline is a GPU OpenCL filter, not a CPU codec; there is no software backend. Rust crate outside the search's C++ language filter.

notes: Real, public harness (scripts/src/benchmark_e2e.py + scripts/configs/benchmark_e2e.toml) with a matched-parameter FFmpeg nlmeans_opencl arm, but first-party, image-only results and missing host/toolchain details keep it at C. tier_reason: docs/README.md and docs/assets/processing-speed.png give first-party relative speeds (fast_vad offline 721x, streaming 129x, webrtcvad 63x, Silero ONNX 1x) on a Ryzen 7700X, but the harness that produced them (bench_py/ and notebooks/, gitignored and absent from the repo) is unpublished and no compiler, flags or absolute timings are given. The public bench_rs/benches/vad_bench.rs only times fast_vad itself on synthetic noise, with no webrtcvad or Silero arm.

corrections.workload: Relative processing speed of voice activity detection on speech audio (AVA-Speech and LibriVAD are the accuracy sets; which audio the speed figure used is not stated), with Silero VAD ONNX as the 1x reference. fast_vad offline (VAD.detect, all frames in parallel with rayon on 16 threads) and streaming (VadStateful, one 32 ms frame at a time) against webrtcvad through its Python binding (webrtcvad-wheels in the dev dependencies). The detectors do different work: fast_vad scores 32 ms (512-sample at 16 kHz) Hann-windowed FFT frames with an 8-band log-energy logistic-regression model, while webrtcvad uses its own model on 10, 20 or 30 ms frames; the frame size used for webrtcvad is not stated.
corrections.caveats: The comparison harness is not published (pyproject.toml excludes bench_py/** and notebooks/**, and .gitignore ignores notebooks/), so how webrtcvad was driven (per-frame Python calls, frame size) cannot be checked; numbers are bar-chart multipliers only, with no absolute timings, compiler or flags. The public bench_rs criterion benches (vad_bench.rs, filterbank_bench.rs) time fast_vad alone on LCG-generated noise. The offline 721x figure uses rayon across all 16 threads of the Ryzen 7700X while webrtcvad is single-threaded, so the about 11.4x offline gap is not per-core; the streaming path (about 2x webrtcvad, derived from page data: 129/63) is the like-for-like single-stream figure. The detectors are different models with different frame sizes, so this is a task-level rather than same-algorithm comparison. On AVA-Speech fast_vad F1 is 0.680 against 0.738 (Silero) and 0.669 (webrtcvad); presets were tuned on LibriVAD. Baseline webrtcvad is not in the FFmpeg, x264, Opus list. Rust crate outside the search's C++ language filter.

tier_reason: README Performance table matches the record exactly and is produced by public code (parity/benches/decode.rs, criterion, with upstream minimp3 built from the parity/minimp3 submodule by parity/build.rs), but the CPU model and rustc version are not stated, so it falls short of A; first-party only.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: C references built by the cc crate in parity/build.rs with opt_level 3 plus -ffp-contract=off and -ftrivial-auto-var-init=zero (clang-cl on MSVC targets; README says clang -O3); minimp3 SIMD build uses its default SSE/NEON intrinsics with MINIMP3_ONLY_MP3 and MINIMP3_FLOAT_OUTPUT, scalar build adds MINIMP3_NO_SIMD. Rust side uses the default cargo bench profile (no profile overrides in the workspace Cargo.toml), wide feature on, no target-cpu flag; rustc version not stated (MSRV 1.89). Reproduce with cargo bench -p nanomp3-parity.
corrections.workload: In-memory MP3 frame decode throughput (criterion, MiB/s of MP3 input, f32 output, decoder created per iteration) on three inputs from parity/benches/decode.rs: 'The Washington Post.mp3' (MPEG-1 48 kHz joint stereo 320 kbps, in nanomp3-core/src/tests), the minimp3 conformance vector M2L3_bitrate_22_all.bit (MPEG-2 LSF 22.05 kHz, all bitrates) and l3-he_mode.bit (mono, short blocks, intensity stereo mix).
corrections.stars_or_usage: 22 stars; 3 forks; crates.io nanomp3 0.2.0 (27,841 downloads, 20,154 recent)
corrections.caveats: Baseline minimp3 is itself a small decoder, not libmpg123 or FFmpeg, and nanomp3 is a port of it, so this is a modest win over its own port target: 6-21 percent over minimp3 SIMD and 12-37 percent over minimp3 scalar (derived from page data). CPU model and rustc version not stated, Windows x86-64 only, three inputs, first-party table. Decoding is bit-exact: parity/tests/parity.rs compares nanomp3's f32 output with minimp3's scalar builds on every conformance vector plus the march file, run in CI on ubuntu x86-64, ubuntu-24.04-arm, windows and macos; minimp3's own SIMD build, the faster C baseline, is not bit-exact with its scalar reference. The C builds use -ftrivial-auto-var-init=zero (zeroing minimp3's otherwise uninitialized per-frame scratch, which nanomp3 also zeroes) and -ffp-contract=off, so they are like-for-like with nanomp3 but may run slower than a stock minimp3 build by an unmeasured margin, which matters at a 6 percent gap. Default i16 rounding differs from minimp3 by design (bug fix; compat mode available); the benchmark uses f32. Comparison is Rust versus C, not C++ std.

notes: All nine numbers in claimed_speedup match the README table; nanomp3 0.1 column shows the earlier release was slower than minimp3 (55.7 vs 71.9 MiB/s). baseline_in_list stays false.
